title: Confidence, cadence bucketing + hysteresis, persist item_stats + fixture unit tests
goal: Complete computeItemStats with steps 8-10 (confidence, cadence bucket, hysteresis) and stand up the persistence orchestration (recompute.ts) that fetches an item's inputs, calls the now-complete pure function, and writes item_stats + item_stats_history -- the last piece before S-15/S-16 can wire triggers to it.
in_scope: Step 8 (confidence): cv = MAD_normalized / median_interval, MAD_normalized = MAD * 1.4826 (standard consistency constant for a normal-distribution-equivalent std-dev estimate; median/MAD from the same post-rejection interval set as step 5, cv=0 when median_interval=0 to avoid division by zero). confidence = clamp((n/(n+3)) * (1 - min(cv,1)), 0, 1), n = post-rejection usable interval count (same n as step 5's shrinkage weight). Implemented literally per working spec Sec5 step 8 -- see acceptance note: the doc's own A5 worked example ('confidence High') does not hold under this literal formula and is corrected in this epic's acceptance text and ledger, not the formula itself (AGENTS.md: working spec wins for algorithm detail over descriptive prose).

Step 9 (bucket): candidateBucket = confidence < 0.35 ? 'unpredictable' : thresholdBucket(intervalEstDays) using the 8 fixed day boundaries (<=1.5 daily, 1.5-4 every_2_3_days, 4-10 weekly, 10-20 fortnightly, 20-45 monthly, 45-135 quarterly, 135-270 half_yearly, 270-500 yearly, >500 unpredictable).

Step 10 (hysteresis): finalBucket = candidateBucket unchanged from previous.cadenceBucket unless intervalEstDays crosses the boundary immediately adjacent to the previous bucket by >15% (interval_est > boundary*1.15 moving to a longer-cadence bucket, or < boundary*0.85 moving to a shorter one). No previous state (first-ever compute) skips hysteresis entirely. Transitions into or out of 'unpredictable' are NOT hysteresised (deliberate scope cut -- 'unpredictable' has two independent trigger conditions, interval>500 and confidence<0.35, with no single numeric boundary a >15%-crossing test can apply to; documented in the ledger, not a gap to silently paper over).
New ComputeItemStatsConfig-adjacent input `previous: PreviousBucketState` (declared in S-14a's types.ts, wired here): { cadenceBucket, intervalEstDays } from the item's prior item_stats row.

Migration: `alter table item_stats add column interval_est_days numeric;` (additive) -- persists step 5's pre-bucketing interval estimate so the next recompute's hysteresis check has a stable prior value to compare against, without re-deriving it from ewma_interval_days + purchase_count (which would silently drift if the category prior or purchase_count changes between recomputes).

lib/predictions/recompute.ts (server-only): recomputeOneItem(catalogItemId, householdId, deps) -- fetches purchase stock_movements (type='purchase', that item, ordered), current item_stats row (for previous bucket/interval_est/rate_correction), category default_prior_days (via catalog_items.category_id), catalog_items.perishability_days, and v_current_stock for the item; calls computeItemStats; upserts item_stats (all columns); inserts one item_stats_history row (stats as jsonb snapshot of the new ItemStats); trims that item's history to the 5 most recent rows.

Migration: `trim_item_stats_history(p_household_id uuid)` Postgres function -- single window-function DELETE keeping the 5 most recent item_stats_history rows per catalog_item_id for the household, callable via supabase.rpc so both the on-commit (single item) and nightly (whole household) paths share one trim call shape.

Items with zero purchase events are skipped entirely by recompute.ts (no item_stats row is written/attempted) -- there's nothing to compute and no meaningful null-stats row is more useful than no row.

Fixture unit tests (throwaway tsx script, working spec Sec12 / Sec11 A5-A7): A5 (day 0/7/14/21, qtyBase omitted so q=0) -> bucket weekly, confidence ~0.50 (Medium), next purchase ~= day 28. A6 (day 0/7/60/67) -> the 60-day gap interval rejected as an outlier (n=3 usable intervals satisfies the lowered n>=3 gate), bucket stays weekly. A7 (2 purchases, 1 usable interval) -> interval_est is prior-dominated (w=1/3), confidence ~0.25 (Learning, <0.35), and per step 9's compound condition the bucket is 'unpredictable' (not a numeric cadence) -- the acceptance's 'prior-dominated' language describes interval_est, not the bucket.
out_of_scope: Wiring recomputeOneItem to any trigger -- on-commit call site and nightly cron are S-16.

Multi-item / whole-household batch recompute (nightly path) -- S-16 builds the batched variant on top of this story's per-item function; this story's recompute.ts only needs to work correctly for one item at a time.
acceptance: Day 0/7/14/21 fixture buckets weekly, confidence Medium (~0.50 under the literal n/(n+3) formula with n=3 usable intervals -- doc's worked example says 'High' but that's prose, not a purpose-backed rule; the formula constant is algorithm detail and wins per AGENTS.md, see ledger), next purchase ~= day 28 (A5, with qtyBase omitted so q=0 and the assertion isolates interval estimation); one outlier interval (vacation/bulk-buy) doesn't move the bucket (A6); 2-purchase fixture (n=1 usable interval) is prior-dominated, confidence Learning (~0.25 <0.35) and therefore bucket=unpredictable by step 9's compound condition, not a numeric cadence bucket (A7); bucket only changes when interval_est crosses the adjacent boundary by >15% (hysteresis; unpredictable transitions are unhysteresised, see ledger); item_stats + item_stats_history (last 5) persisted.
invariants: computeItemStats itself remains pure and DB-free after this story -- all DB access lives in recompute.ts, never inside lib/predictions/computeItemStats.ts.
recompute.ts never writes cadence_override -- that column is exclusively user-set (F11, a later epic's Plan screen) and recompute must never clobber it.

item_stats_history is a debugging aid capped at 5 rows per item (docs/architecture/03-data-model.md), not an audit log -- the trim function enforces this on every recompute, no unbounded growth path exists.
